title: AWS Cloud Security
subtitle: Secure, monitor and respond to incidents on AWS accounts and workloads
audience_line: Security, cloud and operations engineers responsible for AWS environments
certifications: AWS Certified Security – Specialty (SCS-C03), core topics
overview: This programme teaches participants to secure Amazon Web Services environments from identity to incident response. They work with IAM policies and their evaluation logic, govern many accounts with Organizations, service and resource control policies and IAM Identity Center, protect networks and the edge, encrypt data and manage secrets, detect threats and misconfigurations with CloudTrail, Config, GuardDuty, Security Hub CSPM and Inspector, and respond to incidents with playbooks and automated remediation. An overview of the Security – Specialty exam closes the content, and the programme ends with a final project: a deliberately insecure account secured by each team, with a findings report.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Security, cloud and operations engineers responsible for AWS environments

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Core AWS services (course: AWS Cloud Practitioner), or equivalent hands-on use. Core services are not taught again

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 33 h: 27 h of chapters + 6 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs; incident simulations

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: One laptop per participant with the AWS CLI; one AWS Organizations sandbox per team (management and member accounts), provided by the organiser, with a budget alert; detection services and resources disabled or destroyed at the end of each lab to control cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase and a final project with a findings report; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can apply least privilege across accounts, protect networks and data, detect threats and misconfigurations, and respond to an incident on AWS with automated remediation

phases.name: Identity & Governance
phases.focus: Shared responsibility, IAM policies and evaluation, Organizations, federation
phases.intro: Participants start from the security pillar of the Well-Architected Framework, then master the identity layer: how IAM evaluates policies, roles and permission boundaries, access analysis, and multi-account governance with Organizations, service and resource control policies, IAM Identity Center and Cognito. Validated lab: a member account where a service control policy blocks disabling CloudTrail, and developers sign in through IAM Identity Center with a permission set.

chapters.title: Security on AWS
chapters.content: Shared responsibility, the Well-Architected security pillar

chapters.title: IAM in Depth
chapters.content: Policies and evaluation logic, roles, permission boundaries, IAM Access Analyzer

chapters.title: Multi-Account Governance & Federation
chapters.content: Organizations, service control policies and resource control policies, IAM Identity Center, Cognito

phases.name: Infrastructure & Data Protection
phases.focus: VPC security, WAF, Shield, Network Firewall, KMS, Secrets Manager, Macie
phases.intro: Participants protect the network layer with security groups, network ACLs, AWS Network Firewall, WAF and Shield, then protect data with KMS keys and key policies, encryption at rest and in transit, Secrets Manager, ACM certificates and Macie. Validated lab: a web application behind WAF that blocks an injection attempt, with its database encrypted by a customer managed key and its password rotated by Secrets Manager.

chapters.title: Network & Edge Protection
chapters.content: VPC security, security groups and network ACLs, WAF, Shield Standard (Shield Advanced presented, not subscribed), Network Firewall

chapters.title: Protecting Data
chapters.content: KMS, encryption at rest and in transit, Secrets Manager, ACM, Macie

phases.name: Detection, Response & Exam Overview
phases.focus: CloudTrail, Config, GuardDuty, Security Hub CSPM, Inspector, incident response, SCS-C03
phases.intro: Participants turn on the services that show what happens in an account, fix the posture findings, then respond to simulated incidents with playbooks, automated remediation and evidence collection. An overview of the SCS-C03 domains and scenario practice closes the phase. Validated lab: a GuardDuty finding that triggers an EventBridge rule and a Lambda function isolating the compromised instance.

chapters.title: Detection & Posture
chapters.content: CloudTrail, CloudWatch, Config, GuardDuty, Security Hub CSPM, Inspector, patching with Systems Manager

chapters.title: Security – Specialty (SCS-C03) Overview
chapters.content: Exam domains, scenario practice and gap analysis

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A deliberately insecure account, secured and reported
phases.intro: Each team receives an AWS account with deliberately insecure settings, secures it by reusing the phase labs, and presents its findings report as it would to a security officer.

chapters.title: Assess & Fix
chapters.content: Find the weaknesses, apply least-privilege IAM, encryption and logging

chapters.title: Detect & Automate
chapters.content: Enable GuardDuty and Security Hub CSPM, automate one remediation, write the findings report

chapters.title: Report & Review
chapters.content: Present findings, fixes and remaining risks; questions and feedback

project.title: Securing an Insecure AWS Account
project.brief: An AWS account with deliberately insecure settings brought to a secure baseline: least-privilege IAM, encryption, logging, GuardDuty and Security Hub CSPM, and at least one automated remediation, documented in a findings report.
project.stack: AWS: IAM, Organizations, KMS, CloudTrail, Config, GuardDuty, Security Hub CSPM, EventBridge, Lambda, Systems Manager
project.deliverable: Secured account, findings report with fixes and remaining risks, presentation
